claims.statement: The SourceControlProvider interface (packages/control-plane/src/source-control/types.ts) splits its surface into user-authenticated operations (getRepository, createPullRequest) that take a decrypted user token, app-authenticated operations (checkRepositoryAccess, listRepositories, listBranches, getBranchHead, resolveCommit, listTree, readBlob, getPullRequest, generatePushAuth, generateCredentialHelperAuth) that use provider-level credentials configured at construction, and pure builders (buildManualPullRequestUrl, buildGitPushSpec) that perform no I/O.

Provider methods throw SourceControlProviderError carrying an errorType of transient (retryable: HTTP 429, 5xx, and network-shaped failures like fetch failures, timeouts, connection resets, aborts) or permanent (configuration, auth, validation), plus the HTTP status when known; both providers classify errors through the shared fromFetchError helper so retry policy is uniform.

resolveScmProviderFromEnv trims and lower-cases the SCM_PROVIDER value, returns DEFAULT_SCM_PROVIDER (github) when unset or empty, accepts only github/bitbucket/gitlab, and throws a permanent SourceControlProviderError listing supported values otherwise; provider selection comes exclusively from configuration with no auto-detection.

createSourceControlProvider switches on the provider name: github always constructs, gitlab requires GitLab configuration (missing token is a permanent error), bitbucket throws the explicit "SCM provider 'bitbucket' is configured but not implemented." permanent error, and unknown runtime values hit an exhaustive never-guard; the switch makes adding a provider name a compile-time-forced decision.

createSourceControlProviderFromEnv assembles factory config from Env: GitHub gets the GitHub App config, a KV cache store over env.REPOS_CACHE for installation-token caching, and an app-name User-Agent; GitLab config (GITLAB_ACCESS_TOKEN with optional GITLAB_NAMESPACE) is included only when GITLAB_ACCESS_TOKEN is set.

The worker router memoizes the deployment-level SCM resolution in a module-level cachedScmProvider keyed by the raw SCM_PROVIDER value (re-validating only when the env value changes and re-throwing a cached permanent error), and enforceImplementedScmProvider returns 501 Not Implemented for routes whose supportedScmProviders exclude the deployment provider and 500 with the resolver message when the configuration itself is invalid.

Authentication runs before the SCM provider gate — an unauthenticated request to a restricted route gets 401 even on a GitLab deployment — while public routes still surface invalid SCM configuration as 500; both orderings are pinned by router policy tests.

Route policies are pinned as named constants in routes/shared.ts (GITHUB_USER_OR_SERVICE_ROUTE, SCM_AGNOSTIC_* variants, SCM_CREDENTIALS_ROUTE, sandbox-fallback variants); SCM_CREDENTIALS_ROUTE is sandbox-authenticated and is the only route supporting gitlab, while GitHub-specific routes such as ws-token and commit signing are pinned to ["github"].

Provider construction is cheap (no I/O), so Worker routes build one per request via createRouteSourceControlProvider, the Session DO constructs its instance eagerly during runtime initialization so a misconfigured deployment fails session requests before any session state is written, and background consumers (scheduler, automations, image builds) construct per firing or receive the provider injected — resolveSessionRepoId takes it as a thunk so legacy rows carrying a repo_id never construct it.
For existence lookups, a confirmed 404 is absence rather than error: getBranchHead and resolveCommit return null on 404 and throw only for authentication, throttling, and transport failures.

checkRepositoryAccess returns null when the repository is not available to the deployment (not installed for GitHub, inaccessible/archived/no readable default branch for GitLab) and otherwise returns the stable numeric repoId, lower-cased repoOwner/repoName, and defaultBranch; archived repositories are treated as inaccessible on GitHub and GitLab alike.

getPullRequest provides rename/transfer tolerance in both providers: on a 404 with a known stable repositoryExternalId, the provider resolves the repository's current owner/name by id (GitHub's GET /repositories/{id} alias; GitLab's GET /projects/{id}) and retries exactly once, degrading best-effort to the original 404 if resolution fails, and treats the successful read's location as canonical for the returned snapshot.

Providers return only status facts (lifecycleState plus isDraft); consumers derive display state with toDisplayStatus at their own boundary, so a provider result can never carry an inconsistent pair, with the invariant that isDraft is true only while lifecycleState is open.

GitHub models merged as state closed plus merged true, so deriveGitHubPullRequestStatus maps merged terminal-first over a stale draft flag, then closed, then open with isDraft = (draft === true); GitLab has a first-class merged state and its deriveGitLabMergeRequestStatus additionally treats the transient mid-merge locked state as open; both mappers are shared by the user-authed create path and the app-authed read path.

Repository tree and blob reads are pinned to a commit: listTree lists entries reachable from one commit and readBlob reads by the provider blob id from that listing so content cannot drift with the ref; entries are classified by the shared classifyGitTreeEntry (symlinks, submodules, and unknown modes become "other"), listTree reports truncated when a provider cap cuts the listing, and readBlob's maxBytes is a refusal threshold enforced by the shared readResponseBytesWithinLimit helper that cancels oversized bodies rather than buffering them.

The GitHub provider performs user-authenticated getRepository and createPullRequest with the user's Bearer token against api.github.com; createPullRequest maps the response through strict zod schemas (the PR state is a closed enum so schema drift fails the parse), captures headSha, repositoryExternalId from base.repo.id, and providerUpdatedAt, and treats labels and reviewers as best-effort — labels are ensured per-label with a 422 race re-check and any label/reviewer failure is logged without failing PR creation.

All app-authenticated GitHub calls go through one appFetch helper that mints an installation token via getCachedInstallationToken (in-memory plus KV cache over the provider's cacheStore) and sends it as Bearer; a missing appConfig is a permanent error at call time, and generateCredentialHelperAuth uses the with-expiry token getter so the returned expiresAtEpochMs is the installation token's true lifetime.

GitHub's generateCredentialHelperAuth returns username x-access-token (GitHub's HTTPS basic-auth username for installation tokens), a freshly minted installation token as the password, and the token's absolute expiry as expiresAtEpochMs.

GitHub's buildManualPullRequestUrl produces https://github.com/{owner}/{name}/pull/new/{base}...{head} with every component encodeURIComponent-encoded wholesale, and buildGitPushSpec produces a credential-bearing remote URL https://x-access-token:{token}@github.com/{owner}/{name}.git with a redactedRemoteUrl twin (<redacted>) for safe logging, the refspec {sourceRef}:refs/heads/{targetBranch}, and repoOwner/repoName/force fields.

GitHubSourceControlProvider exposes GitHub-only methods outside the portable interface — getPullRequestFeedback (PR comments and reviews with ownership checks binding the object to the requested PR path) and hasPullRequestWritePermission — consumed by the feedback/autofix pipelines; the SourceControlProvider interface is the portable surface, not the whole provider.

The GitLab provider is PAT-only: one deployment-configured Personal Access Token (GITLAB_ACCESS_TOKEN, read_api scope for reads and api scope for writes; optional GITLAB_NAMESPACE group scope) authenticates every call to https://gitlab.com/api/v4 with Bearer, and the constructor rejects a blank token permanently so a misconfigured GitLab deployment fails at provider construction.

The GitLab provider handles nested groups by URL-encoding the whole project path for API calls (owner/name to owner%2Fname) and mapping the project's namespace.full_path — not the bare namespace — to owner, so group/subgroup round-trips through owner/name lookups; a missing default_branch in the repository response is a permanent "token cannot read repository code" error because the token can see the project but not its code.

GitLab merge-request creation adapts GitHub-shaped config: drafts become a "Draft: " title prefix, labels are joined into one field, and reviewer assignment is unsupported (username-to-ID resolution would need an extra API call per reviewer) so it is warned and ignored; the create response captures iid, web_url, the API self link, headSha, project_id as repositoryExternalId, and updated_at.

GitLab listRepositories hits /groups/{ns}/projects with include_subgroups=true when a namespace is configured, else /projects?membership=true, always archived=false, using the project path (URL slug) rather than the display name and dropping projects without a default branch; listTree paginates at per-page 100 and caps at MAX_TREE_PAGES = 20 pages before reporting truncated, reports sizeBytes as always null because GitLab's tree endpoint reports no blob sizes, and treats a 404 on a scoped subtree path (GitLab 17.7+) as an empty listing.

GitLab's generatePushAuth returns the PAT itself (authType pat) since there is no app installation to broker with, and generateCredentialHelperAuth returns username oauth2 with the PAT as password and a fixed one-hour expiry (GITLAB_CREDENTIAL_HELPER_TTL_MS) because GitLab PATs expose no expiry the control plane could read.

GitLab's buildManualPullRequestUrl builds https://gitlab.com/{owner}/{name}/-/merge_requests/new?merge_request[source_branch]=…&merge_request[target_branch]=… with the project web path encoded per segment so nested group separators survive as literal slashes, and buildGitPushSpec builds https://oauth2:{token}@gitlab.com/{owner}/{name}.git with deliberately literal (unencoded) path segments because GitLab project paths are URL-safe and git clients expect literal segments, plus the same redacted twin and refspec shape as GitHub.

Repository owners may contain '/', and the stack handles this: parseRepositoryFullName splits an owner/name string on the last slash (rejecting empty owner segments) so group/subgroup/web parses as owner group/subgroup and name web; encodeRepositoryPathSegments encodes the owner as one route segment (group%2Fsubgroup/web%20app); route patterns bind :owner to a single [^/]+ segment and extractRepoParams decodes it via decodeRepositoryPathSegments, which rejects an encoded slash in the name and non-canonical encodings with 400.

resolveGitHubCredentialAuthority selects the credential store backing a user's GitHub identity: a browser-session user resolves through the Better Auth provider-account client with the linked-account list validated per request (malformed list or an account owned by a different user throws "GitHub account authority is corrupt", and more than one linked GitHub account throws "User resolves to multiple GitHub provider accounts"), a user with no linked GitHub account resolves to githubAccount null (falling back to the shared App bot), and only service actors retain the legacy D1 token-store authority — a user principal without browser-session provenance throws rather than silently downgrading.

The credential authority is consumed by resolveGitHubEnrichmentForRequest (legacy path reads the D1 user_scm_tokens store; browser-session path fetches the access token through the account client and encrypts it with the deployment's token-encryption key before it touches session state), and both session-create and session-prompt resolve the authority only when the deployment provider is github — on GitLab deployments the GitHub enrichment path is skipped entirely.

SessionPullRequestService orchestrates PR creation: it calls generatePushAuth() for the push credential, builds the GitPushSpec for the target repository and head branch, and hands it to SandboxPushService, which performs the sandbox protocol's only request/response exchange — a push command over the sandbox WebSocket settled by push_complete/push_error events with a 360-second timeout, where no connected sandbox counts as success on the assumption the branch was pushed manually; GitPushSpec.repoOwner/repoName select the checkout in multi-repo sandboxes.

PR creation prefers the prompting user's OAuth token for attribution and falls back to the app/PAT token (the path for Linear-spawned sessions and users without a linked GitHub account); the resulting provider result is mapped through a single PullRequestSnapshot mapping into the DO artifact and the best-effort D1 authority record, and creation is serialized per target repository by in-memory claims on the DO instance.

POST /sessions/:id/scm-credentials is a sandbox-authenticated route (github + gitlab only) whose handler wraps generateCredentialHelperAuth in ScmCredentialsService, which validates the response (non-empty username/password, finite expiresAtEpochMs in the future, otherwise 500), maps permanent provider errors to 500 and transient ones to 502 so the sandbox helper exits non-zero and the next git operation retries, and never logs the returned password; integration tests pin the full sandbox-auth → DO → service → provider chain including rejection of user/service credentials.

scmCloneIdentity maps each provider to a sandbox clone identity — host, clone username, and secret hosts (github.com/x-access-token, gitlab.com/oauth2, bitbucket.org/x-token-auth) — applied to sandbox env as VCS_HOST/VCS_CLONE_USERNAME, matching the credential-helper usernames the providers' generateCredentialHelperAuth implementations return.

The manual-PR path stays part of the provider contract: manual-PR branch artifacts (mode manual_pr with a createPrUrl) are rendered as Create-PR buttons by the Slack bot, the sandbox's create-pull-request tool can surface a manual envelope (kind manual with createPrUrl) when the create response signals the manual path, and prior manual branch artifacts are ignored when a later request creates a real PR.

Two capabilities degrade explicitly by provider: managed-skill imports consume only the RepositoryReader subset of the interface (checkRepositoryAccess, resolveCommit, listTree, readBlob), and commit signing is GitHub-only — on non-GitHub deployments the sandbox commit-signing endpoints return an explicit { enabled: false } for GET and 409 for POST so unsupported providers degrade safely instead of failing sessions.

ADR-0001 pins the deployment architecture: single provider per deployment selected by SCM_PROVIDER with no per-session provider state persisted (PR artifact metadata deliberately has no provider field), fail-fast 501 responses for unimplemented providers, provider-specific PR URL construction, push-transport construction, and sandbox credential-helper auth confined to provider implementations with direct GitHub API base URL usage limited to approved auth/provider modules, and guardrails enforced through code review plus focused provider/factory tests.

docs/provider-contribution-checklist.md is the extension guide for adding a provider: implementation under packages/control-plane/src/source-control/providers, an explicit factory case in createSourceControlProvider, the name recognized by the SCM_PROVIDER resolver, user-authenticated repository lookup and PR creation plus push auth, buildManualPullRequestUrl, buildGitPushSpec, and generateCredentialHelperAuth implemented via provider methods (helper auth being a prerequisite for enabling helper-backed sandbox git auth), with test requirements covering factory selection/unsupported behavior, manual PR URL building, push spec building, credential-helper auth, basic API mapping, and non-regression of create-PR branch consistency and Slack manual-PR button tests.

The /repos listing route builds a provider per request via createRouteSourceControlProvider, calls listRepositories(), enriches the result with D1 repo metadata, and caches the enriched list in KV under repos:list:v2 with a 5-minute fresh window and 1-hour TTL; a permanent provider error with no HTTP status is treated as "provider not configured" rather than a fetch failure.
